correctness.rationale: Strict convexity on all independent simple-wheel conductances proves uniqueness and justifies dihedral reduction. Exact wheel Laplacian eigenvalues give a strictly convex one-variable objective; the first derivative at the rim-free endpoint equals n²t/(n+1)-2n, and the second derivative at the critical price is 4(n-2)>0. Fixed-price minimizer convergence follows from uniform convergence away from zero spoke weight and a divergence exclusion at the boundary. At fixed n, the derivative equation with the exact inverse-cycle-spectrum sum gives the stated square-root cheap-rim law. The 187 finite checks include exact rational full-matrix traces, but are not substituted for proof.

value.rationale: Different prices of radial and circumferential connections motivate precisely the rim-removal question. The sharp \(t_c(n)=2+2/n\) and equality uniqueness classify when all n physically available rim edges must be eliminated in a globally optimized network. A finite-order critical amplitude, a size-dependent shift to the limiting price two, an exact asymptotic performance profile, and noncommuting cheap-price/network-size limits give structural design information not contained in a generic optimizer or an arbitrary parameter slice.
